scoring_limitation.candidate_mass_is: sum of normalized label-prefix scores WITHOUT a termination event; NOT a literal probability mass -- overlapping candidate strings can sum above 1
scoring_limitation.other_mass_is: clamped to zero when the candidate score sum reaches or passes 1 -- the shared scorer computes max(0.0, 1 - candidate_score_sum) in rv.build_candidate_summary -- and is NOT complementary probability mass: a zero here says the overlapping prefixes summed to at least one, not that nothing lies outside the candidate set
scoring_limitation.consequence: normalized candidate-score comparisons and gated distances remain useful and comparable to every existing artifact, but any threshold on candidate_mass (e.g. the frozen min_candidate_mass=0.99 interpretability criterion) is a threshold on a SCORE SUM, not on a probability

report_layer_naming.cached_row_records_are_named: candidate_mass / other_mass, UNCHANGED: renaming a stored field would quarantine a finished sweep
report_layer_naming.frozen_criterion_key_is: gx.PASS_CRITERIA['min_candidate_mass'], UNCHANGED: the criterion is the project's own, not this report's
report_layer_naming.why: a report field called *_mass would assert a probability mass the scorer never measured, so the report layer names the quantity it actually holds; the value, the threshold and the measurement are untouched by the naming

scoring_limitation.termination_diagnostic: route-h rows record eos_prob_after_parsed: P(EOS | prompt + parsed label), a termination-aware reading of the same output; diagnostic only -- no criterion, gate or distance reads it
scoring_limitation.resolution_options: (a) add termination-aware scoring to the shared library: changes the measurement and breaks comparability with every canonical artifact on disk; (b) keep the frozen prefix scorer with this documented semantics plus the EOS diagnostic (CHOSEN)

prompt_support_profile.criterion: a model is on support for a template when the min of the candidate score sum over its own rows for that template is >= the frozen gx.PASS_CRITERIA['min_candidate_mass'] = 0.99
prompt_support_profile.reading: off-support templates are ones where the model's output score sum has left the candidate space, so a renormalized distance there compares two artifacts rather than two behaviors; where the never-edited baseline is off support too, the collapse is a property of how the route was trained and this panel cannot attribute it to the edit.  This profile describes WHICH MODELS leave the candidate space; whether a given Delta_retrain may be quoted is decided per comparison, in distance_to_oracle_by_template[*].per_target[*].interpretable

claims.scope: every number in this report was measured on the 6 pre-frozen prompt templates (canonical, concise_paraphrase, question_form, instruction_form, format_variation, distractor) over the 30-label route-h candidate space and the 12-code route-g candidate space, dataset salmu, 12 identities; the panel was frozen and committed before any model was evaluated, and no template, threshold or recipe was chosen using it.  The candidate and other quantities are normalized label-prefix SCORE SUMS without a termination event, not literal probability masses (see scoring_limitation), so the report layer names them *_score_sum while the cached rows keep the project-wide candidate_mass field; every threshold applied to them, including the frozen min_candidate_mass=0.99 criterion, is a score-sum criterion
claims.route_h_prompt_support: route h prompt support (read this before any other route-h number): 1 of the 6 templates carry an interpretable retraining comparison for at least one edited cell [canonical 63/63 cells].  A comparison is interpretable when the edit and matched_retrain rows clear the frozen min_candidate_mass=0.99 criterion and the loo_retrain row clears the 0.01 distance gate; loo is held to the gate alone because it never saw the target mapping and its drift there is the deletion reference the project's own oracle fit gate already expects, so requiring 0.99 of it would apply the criterion to the one row the project exempts.  The never-edited baseline_h is off support on 5 of 6 templates [concise_paraphrase (1/1 models), question_form (1/1 models), instruction_form (1/1 models), format_variation (1/1 models), distractor (1/1 models)], reaching a minimum candidate score sum of 0.0003 away from canonical, where its strict accuracy is 1.0000 on canonical and at best 0.083 on the other 5.  0 template(s) are off support for edited models but not for the baseline: prompt sensitivity in this sweep is a property of how route h is TRAINED and the panel cannot attribute it to the edit.
claims.route_h: route h (code -> alias): Delta_retrain = D(edit, loo_retrain) - D(edit, matched_retrain) is interpreted only where the compared rows support it, which is 1 of the 6 templates [canonical 63/63 cells]; there it stays positive in 63 of 63 cells with a worst case of 1.1237, against 1.1237 on the canonical prompt alone, so the retraining-equivalence finding is established on the canonical prompt alone, where the matched-vs-LOO result replicates in 63 of 63 cells; none of the 5 held-out prompt forms provides an interpretable extension, because the never-edited baseline route itself loses strict accuracy (1.0000 on canonical, at best 0.083 on the other 5) and candidate-score support (minimum 0.0003 away from canonical).  The unrestricted worst case over all 6 templates is -1.1995 with the sign holding in 0 of 63 cells, but the templates that make it worse are off support, where a renormalized distance compares two artifacts rather than two behaviors, so those values are reported and not interpreted.  Worst-case strict desired-label accuracy on transformation targets is 0.0000 and worst-case hard source leakage is 0.3333
claims.route_g_baseline: route g baseline prompt sensitivity (no intervention): the frozen g_X_to_C router's code accuracy over 12 held-out test images ranges from 0.0000 (worst template: concise_paraphrase) to 0.8333, a maximum template spread of 0.8333; six-template consistency (the same code however it is asked) is 0.0000
claims.route_g_cross_route_spillover: route g edit-induced collateral (confirmatory; no intervention on g): Delta_g = M_g(h_adapter) - M_g(h_baseline) over the identical panel reaches a worst-template prediction-flip rate of 0.0000 and a worst-template code-accuracy change of 0.0000 across 15 h-side adapters; the null expectation is that an h-targeted edit leaves route-g behavior approximately unchanged relative to baseline_h.  Descriptively, replacing the frozen image->code router with ANY h adapter moves behavior by up to 1.0000 worst-template flip rate -- task-adapter replacement, not edit attribution -- and the frozen router's own PP2 accuracy remains the absolute route-g capability ceiling.  Architecturally the pipeline executes frozen g and the h adapter sequentially and the g checkpoint is unchanged, so route-g preservation rests on checkpoint identity, with Delta_g as the empirical probe
not_claimed: no intervention of any kind was applied to the visual router -- no edit, no unlearning run, no g-specific matched or LOO retraining -- so no route-g number describes one

frozen-g comparisons are DESCRIPTIVE cross-task adapter behavior: loading any h adapter in place of the image->code router changes the routed model by itself, so no frozen-g delta is evidence about editing; the confirmatory collateral statistic is Delta_g against baseline_h

distances between h-side adapters measured on route-g prompts are reported as g_spillover_reference_distance, a cross-route reference comparison; they are not oracle distances and support no claim about the visual router
no claim reaches beyond the 6 evaluated templates or the recorded candidate spaces: a prompt outside the panel is unmeasured, not passing
no threshold, gate, promotion criterion or training recipe in this repository changes as a result of this panel
the panel is a held-out behavioral evaluation; it selects no model, no template and no checkpoint
